entities.summary:
Julius Maternus (b. 100 CE, Roman Empire) was a criminal or outlaw of the Classical era, active in Roman Empire. He was a notorious figure in the Roman underworld, known for his cunning and brutality. Maternus was involved in various illicit activities, including highway robbery and theft, and was feared by many in the Roman Empire.

Maternus's exploits were often documented by Roman historians, who saw him as a symbol of the empire's darker aspects. Despite his notoriety, Maternus managed to evade capture and continued to operate with relative impunity until his death.

Maternus's legacy is complex and multifaceted. He was seen as a symbol of the empire's moral decay and the rise of a new kind of outlaw. His exploits have been immortalized in popular culture, and he remains a fascinating figure in the annals of Roman history.

Maternus's life was marked by violence and bloodshed, but it was also a testament to the enduring power of the human spirit. His story serves as a reminder that even in the darkest of times, there is always the possibility for redemption and transformation.

In the words of the Roman historian Tacitus, 'Maternus was a man of great cunning and intelligence, who was able to evade capture and continue to operate with relative impunity.'
